why_this_run: Two rule-picked rounds have ended level, and each produced procedures from what every arm missed: WEB-23 from the first, WEB-24 and WEB-25 from the second. Whether that compounds into a lead is an empirical question with two data points and no answer. This round is the answer: cases nobody here has seen, with those three procedures already in the corpus before anyone knew the cases existed.

case_selection.rule: the most recent reviewed advisories matching the filter, in API order, keeping those with a fix commit in the project's own repository
case_selection.population: 30 reviewed high advisories for maven, newest first, exactly as the API returned them
case_selection.ecosystem_changed_on_purpose: Round 2's provenance recorded, before its results existed, that the rule had returned three advisories from ONE repository and that fixing this was the first thing to do next. Maven was chosen for that reason and for no other; it returned three advisories from TWO repositories and three different classes.

the_test: The three procedures written from the previous rounds' misses are in the corpus and neither of the other arms has them. If they generalise, this is where it shows; if the round ties again, that is three rounds of parity and the honest reading is that the corpus does not lead on code nobody here selected.

classes.GHSA-45ph-gxxr-gwgw: privilege escalation from edit to script right - authorization, the family WEB-24 and WEB-25 came from
classes.GHSA-68mj-5wr7-6fgg: oversized length triggers unchecked allocation - the family WEB-23 came from, though not the same shape: here there is no declared limit at all rather than a limit nothing enforces

arms.treatment: the corpus as it ships after WEB-23, WEB-24 and WEB-25
arms.control: the target, an output schema, and one instruction - senior application security engineer, own judgement, own method
arms.competitor: google/mantis at 5f76be0 (Apache-2.0), followed as written; nothing from it copied here

scoring.class_level: an independent context that sees only the advisory text and the finding text, with opaque ids and an order fixed by a hash unrelated to the arm
scoring.publication: every arm's result is published, including a third tie
